questions.question: Look at those dark heavy clouds covering the sky! It ______ rain very soon.
questions.explanation: 'be going to' is used to make predictions based on present, clear physical evidence (such as dark clouds in the sky).

questions.question: In the Unit 4 reading text on Tourism, what is the closest synonym of the word 'indispensable'?
questions.explanation: 'Indispensable' means absolutely essential, vital, or necessary for a particular purpose.

questions.question: The tourist guide gave us ______ useful information about the historical obelisks of Axum.
questions.explanation: 'Some' is used in affirmative declarative statements with uncountable nouns like 'information'.

questions.question: Which of the following compound nouns is formed by combining 'verb + noun'?
questions.explanation: 'Dining room' is formed by combining the verb participle 'dining' with the noun 'room' (Section 4.4.1).

questions.question: Ethiopia is ______ rich in natural and cultural heritages that millions of international tourists visit every year.
questions.explanation: 'So + adjective + that clause' is used to express cause and result when modifying an adjective alone ('rich').

questions.question: Complete the dialogue: Habtamu: 'The reception phone is ringing loudly in the office.' Fikirte: 'Don't worry, I ______ answer it.'
questions.explanation: 'Will' is used for spontaneous decisions made at the exact moment of speaking, whereas 'be going to' expresses prior plans.

questions.question: Community-based tourism allows local residents to sell handmade products, thereby increasing regional revenue. What is the contextual meaning of 'revenue'?

options.text: Total income or money generated by an state, business, or community
Total financial losses incurred during a trip
Fines paid to traffic law enforcement officers

questions.explanation: Contextually, 'revenue' refers to the total income or yield of money received by a community or organization from sales and services.

questions.question: Simien Mountains National Park features ______ an evergreen scenery that the flow of tourists increases steadily.
questions.explanation: 'Such + article + adjective + noun + that' ('such an evergreen scenery that') is used when modifying a noun phrase.

questions.question: Did the tour operator find ______ available hotel rooms in Gondar? No, he couldn't find ______.
questions.explanation: 'Any' is standardly used in general questions and in negative statements.

questions.question: Foreign tourists highly appreciate the genuine hospitality offered by Ethiopian host communities. What is the synonym of 'hospitality'?

options.text: Kindness and courtesy in welcoming strangers

questions.explanation: 'Hospitality' is defined as kindness, warmth, and courtesy in welcoming and entertaining guests or strangers.

questions.question: According to the reading passage on Tourism, what defines 'community-based tourism'?

options.text: Tourism controlled exclusively by international luxury resort companies
Tourism where members of local communities produce crafts and services to directly earn additional income
Government programs that restrict local residents from entering tourist parks
Free accommodation sponsored by foreign embassies

questions.explanation: Community-based tourism involves local residents manufacturing and selling local products to tourists, earning income directly for community development.

questions.question: Select the sentence that uses result clause structures ('so... that' or 'such... that') INCORRECTLY:

options.text: The waterfall created so beautiful a sound that everyone stopped to listen.
It was such a rainy season that I bought a thick jacket.
Girma is such a far-sighted person that he has never been exposed to serious problems.
The film was such interesting that everyone was talking about it on their way home.

questions.explanation: Option D is incorrect because 'interesting' is an adjective standing alone before 'that' without a noun; it requires 'so' ('so interesting that'), not 'such'.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses apostrophes to demonstrate SEPARATE ownership of different books by Belete and Ayele?

options.text: This is Belete and Ayele's book.
These are Belete's and Ayele's books.
These are Belete and Ayele's books.
This is Beletes' and Ayeles' book.

questions.explanation: To indicate separate ownership by two individuals, the possessive apostrophe + 's' is added to each individual name ('Belete's and Ayele's books'). Joint ownership attaches apostrophe + 's' only to the last name.

questions.question: 'If there are pick-pockets, brigands, or bandits fighting in forests, no tourist will attempt to visit that area.' What is the contextual meaning of 'brigands'?

options.text: Members of a gang of bandits or outlaws that attack and rob travelers

questions.explanation: Contextually in security discussions within Unit 4, 'brigands' refers to violent outlaws or bandits who rob travelers.

questions.question: Reorder the jumbled clauses into a syntactically correct sentence expressing cause and result: 'so / that / the / waterfall / spectacular / twin / views / were / offered / visitors / unbelievable / satisfaction / .'

options.text: The twin falls were so spectacular that the views offered visitors unbelievable satisfaction.
The views were so spectacular that twin falls offered unbelievable satisfaction visitors.
Unbelievable satisfaction was so spectacular that visitors offered the twin falls views.
So spectacular were the views that twin falls offered visitors unbelievable satisfaction.

questions.explanation: Standard sentence structure for 'so... that' result clauses follows: Subject ('The twin falls') + Verb ('were') + 'so' + Adjective ('spectacular') + 'that' + Result Clause ('the views offered visitors unbelievable satisfaction').
